The L2 is saturated at 96.9% while L1 hit rate is 0%, meaning every load misses L1 and hammers L2. The CPIStall rule shows 44.1 cycles per warp stalled on L1TEX, accounting for 58.1% of all stall cycles. The scheduler has 80.09% idle slots due to these stalls. Adding tl.max_contiguous and tl.multiple_of hints on the load pointer tells the Triton compiler the x-dimension access is aligned and contiguous in blocks of XBLOCK, enabling 128-bit (float4) vectorized loads instead of scalar 32-bit loads. This reduces the number of memory transactions by 4x and alleviates L2 pressure. Additionally, adding @triton.autotune explores tile configurations that may improve L2 reuse for the strided load dimension.
